text:
Alice Nguyen: quick heads-up — we've got a customer escalation: streaming responses frequently end with a broken pipe and are being counted as 5xx in telemetry. seeing spike starting ~2025-03-01 14:12 UTC. sample customer: acct_9Xx, request ids attached.

Carlos Rivera: customer reports: UI shows 'Server error' after a few tokens, but raw server logs show connection reset. they want to know if this is on our side.

Mateo Diaz: can you paste the request_id and a snippet of the gateway logs? I'll take initial triage.

Alice Nguyen: pasted below. noticed this is only for streaming endpoints (/v1/stream and /v1/chat with stream=true). non-streaming calls are fine.

--- log snippet ---
```
REQUEST_ID=r-0a1b2c3d
TIMESTAMP=2025-03-01T14:12:41Z
CLIENT_IP=3.18.54.12
UPSTREAM=model-03
GATEWAY=gw-06
REQUEST=POST /v1/chat?stream=true
RESPONSE_STATUS=200
ERROR=write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->3.18.54.12:52081: write: broken pipe
NGINX_ERRNO=104
```
--- end ---

Priya Patel: that looks like the gateway succeeded in getting tokens from the runtime, started streaming chunks, then the client terminated the TCP connection mid-stream. gateway is returning 200 to the runtime but logs show a write error. question: why are these counted as 5xx in our metrics?

Elena Kim: I saw a pattern in dashboards: when gateway sees a socket write failure it translates to an internal error code and increments our 5xx counter (we treat write errors as upstream failures).

Mateo Diaz: ok. two distinct issues: 1) classification of client aborts as server 5xx (incorrect), 2) customers see opaque "Server error" in UI and assume our inference died. we should: surface a clearer error to the user, and change metric classification so client disconnects get a client-abort code (like 499) and not counted against SLO.

Carlos Rivera: any mitigation we can give customers right now? some are hitting this repeatedly at scale.

Priya Patel: temporary mitigations: 
- disable streaming (stream=false) for critical paths — will not break, but increases latency and cost.
- increase client-side keepalive and retry logic so clients don't drop connections during long responses.
- implement server-side graceful close: attempt to mark request as client-abort and avoid bumping 5xx alerts.

Mateo Diaz: repro steps for eng to simulate locally:
1) run a long-running streaming response (e.g., prompt that produces many tokens)
2) connect with curl, then kill the client mid-stream

Example:
```
# start a streaming request
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"tell me a long story"}],"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
# in another terminal sleep 2s then kill the curl process to simulate client abort
sleep 2; pkill -f "curl -v -N"
```
This reproduces the write: broken pipe line in gateway logs.

Elena Kim: also saw an edge case where some SDKs set Connection: close or use proxies that aggressively close idle sockets. those clients get counted as our failures today.

Mateo Diaz: created INC-2209 and assigned to eng-runtime and eng-oncall. tagging @Priya for runtime changes.

SRE Bot: INC-2209 created by mateo, severity P2, linked to alert group streaming-5xx-spike.

Priya Patel: plan proposal:
- short term (hotfix, 4h): detect EPIPE / write errors and classify as client_aborted; do not increment 5xx SLO counters; add a telemetry flag so we can count aborted streams separately.
- medium (2d): add integration test that simulates client aborts and verifies classification.
- long (2w): update SDK docs and add guidance for keepalive and retry patterns.

Mateo Diaz: sounds good. Can we also surface a clearer error payload to the customer when the gateway detects client abort so support can tell them the difference? e.g., return 499-ish body or a header X-Client-Abort: true so frontends can show 'Client disconnected' instead of 'Server error'.

Priya Patel: yes. we'll add header and also set response code to 499 when client closed politely. caveat: many proxies don't forward 499, but it will help modern clients.

Carlos Rivera: I'll send customer-facing copy once we have the header or recommended mitigation. want to avoid telling them to just disable streaming unless necessary.

Mateo Diaz: pushing hotfix now. small patch in gateway: change metric increment condition and emit X-Client-Abort header when socket write fails with EPIPE/EINVAL.

Deploy Bot: deployment started: gw-hotfix/aborts-classify at 2025-03-01T18:05:12Z by mateo. CI passed.

Deploy Bot: deployment complete: gw-hotfix/aborts-classify -> 100% on gw-cluster-us-east-1 at 2025-03-01T18:09:34Z.

Priya Patel: hotfix merged and deployed. I also added a toggle feature flag (telemetry.client_abort_classify) default ON. will follow up with integration test tomorrow.

SRE Bot: incident update: INC-2209 status changed to mitigated. 5xx alert rate dropped to baseline after deployment.

Alice Nguyen: customer informed; they confirmed error messages are clearer and no longer seeing 'Server error' in their UI for aborted streams.

Elena Kim: follow-ups:
- ENG-RUNTIME to add integration test (owner: Priya)
- ENG-DEVEX to update SDK docs (owner: Elena)
- SUPPORT to update KB article and escalation playbook (owner: Alice)

Mateo Diaz: estimate: 2 engineer-days total for tests + docs. assigning in JIRA to ENG-2345.

Carlos Rivera: customer happy with mitigations; leaving for longer-term SDK guidance. thanks team! :tada:

Alice Nguyen: closing thread — will reopen if we see reoccurrence.
